# Cyber Elementary

> Cyber security, online safety, digital citizenship and AI safety education for elementary students (grades 3-6): lesson plan books, skills workbooks and free video lessons for teachers and homeschool families. Created by Mark W. Mattei (25+ years in cybersecurity) and published by Baldwin Terney Press LLC.

## Curriculum

- [Curriculum overview, grades 3-6](https://www.cyberelementary.com/curriculum.html): 36 lessons in 4 units, 30–40 minutes each, with scope & sequence and FAQ
- Grade-level editions: one lesson plan book each for grades 3, 4, 5 and 6 (quiz length by grade: 3: 4 questions, 4: 5 questions, 5: 5 questions, 6: 6 questions), plus a complete edition covering all four grades

### Cyber Security Basics (Lessons 1-9)

- Lesson 1: Creating Strong Passwords — Your Digital Lock and Key
- Lesson 2: Keeping Devices and Software Updated — Giving Your Digital Tools Their Checkup
- Lesson 3: Recognizing Phishing Emails and Messages — Don't Take the Bait
- Lesson 4: Understanding Malware and Viruses — Germs for Your Computer
- Lesson 5: Safe Wi-Fi and Network Habits — Locking Your Digital Front Door
- Lesson 6: Protecting Personal Information/Data — Your Digital Treasure Chest
- Lesson 7: Two-Factor Authentication Basics — A Second Lock on Your Account
- Lesson 8: Backing Up Important Data — Your Digital Safety Net
- Lesson 9: Physical Device Security — Protecting the Hardware, Not Just the Data

### Online Safety (Lessons 10-18)

- Lesson 10: Sharing Information Safely Online — Think Before You Post
- Lesson 11: Understanding Digital Footprints — The Trail You Leave Online
- Lesson 12: Cyberbullying — Recognizing and Responding
- Lesson 13: Safe Social Media Habits — Using Apps the Smart Way
- Lesson 14: Stranger Danger Online — Not Everyone Is Who They Say They Are
- Lesson 15: Evaluating Trustworthy Websites — Not Everything Online Is True
- Lesson 16: Screen Time and Digital Balance — Making Room for Everything You Love
- Lesson 17: Safe Online Gaming — Playing Smart with Others
- Lesson 18: Reporting Inappropriate Content — Speaking Up the Right Way

### Digital Citizenship & Communication (Lessons 19-27)

- Lesson 19: Being Kind Online (Digital Citizenship) — The Golden Rule Goes Digital
- Lesson 20: Understanding Copyright and Plagiarism — Giving Credit Where It's Due
- Lesson 21: Email and Messaging Etiquette — Writing Like a Pro
- Lesson 22: Video Chat and Webcam Safety — Mind What's in the Frame
- Lesson 23: Understanding Cookies and Trackers — The Websites That Remember You
- Lesson 24: Public vs. Private Information — Drawing the Line
- Lesson 25: Recognizing Scams and Too-Good-To-Be-True Offers — 
- Lesson 26: Safe Online Shopping Basics — Buying Smart with a Trusted Adult
- Lesson 27: Digital Footprint Cleanup — Tidying Up Your Online Trail

### AI Security & AI Safety (Lessons 28-36)

- Lesson 28: What Is Artificial Intelligence? — Meeting Our New Digital Helper
- Lesson 29: How AI Chatbots Work — Talking to a Very Good Guesser
- Lesson 30: Recognizing AI-Generated Content — Is That Picture or Video Even Real?
- Lesson 31: AI Bias and Fairness — Why AI Isn't Always Neutral
- Lesson 32: Privacy with AI Tools and Voice Assistants — Who's Listening?
- Lesson 33: Safe and Responsible AI Use for Homework — A Helper, Not a Cheat Sheet
- Lesson 34: AI Misinformation and Fact-Checking — Don't Believe Everything You See
- Lesson 35: Protecting Personal Data from AI Systems — Guarding Your Information
- Lesson 36: Being a Responsible AI Citizen — Bringing It All Together

## Videos

- [Video lessons](https://www.cyberelementary.com/videos.html): a free companion video for each of the 36 lessons, plus one compilation per unit (YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/@CyberElementary)

## Articles for parents and teachers

- [How to Tell If a Picture or Video Was Made by AI](https://www.cyberelementary.com/blog-how-to-tell-if-an-image-or-video-is-ai.html): No single trick proves a picture or video is real. Here's a quick routine for parents, teachers and kids: AI labels, Content Credentials, reverse image search, and a simple Pause-Check-Ask habit.
- [Chatbot Privacy for Kids: What's Safe to Share and What Isn't](https://www.cyberelementary.com/blog-chatbot-privacy-for-kids.html): Kids should treat a chatbot like a stranger who writes everything down. What never to share, what's fine to ask, red flags to watch for, age rules and parental controls.
- [A Parent's Checklist for a Child's First Phone or Tablet](https://www.cyberelementary.com/blog-first-phone-checklist.html): Most of the protection comes from the first hour of setup. A step-by-step checklist: child accounts, screen time, contacts, privacy, passwords, family rules and check-ins.
- [AI and Teen Mental Health](https://www.cyberelementary.com/blog-ai-and-teen-mental-health.html): AI is now part of everyday teen life — from study apps to chatbots and social feeds. Here's how it affects emotional well-being, and practical steps for teens, parents, and schools to use it more safely.
